rules.title: No-fault eviction relocation assistance and Declaration of Intent to Evict filing (RSO & JCO)
rules.requirement: Before evicting tenants from RSO or JCO units for a no-fault reason, the landlord must pay relocation assistance and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD. The termination notice may be served only after the Declaration is filed, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after it is served.
rules.coverage_text: Tenant not-at-fault evictions from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Listed no-fault reasons include owner, relative or resident manager occupancy; demolition, commercial conversion or removal from rental use (Ellis Act for RSO units); compliance with a government Order to Vacate; HUD-owned property recovery before sale; Residential Hotel conversion or demolition; conversion to affordable housing; and demolition or conversion to condominiums, stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels and commercial uses regardless of RSO or JCO status.
rules.exemptions: Landlords are exempt from paying relocation assistance when evicting a resident manager to replace them with another resident manager (a Manager-Tenant receiving free or reduced rent with no other compensation may be entitled to relocation), or when required to evict due to hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster not caused by the landlord's negligence. A landlord may offset the tenant's accumulated rent against relocation assistance, unless the assistance is owed because termination is required by a governmental agency order to vacate or to comply with an order for an unpermitted dwelling.
rules.citation: LAMC 151.09.A, 165.03 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance and Just Cause Ordinance)
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO. In an action to recover possession, the tenant may raise the landlord's failure to provide relocation assistance as an affirmative defense; tenants may also file a complaint with LAHD or seek a private right of action.
rules.quoted_span: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO. Notices to terminate tenancy can only be served on the tenant after the landlord files the Declaration with LAHD, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after it is served.

rules.title: Relocation assistance amounts for no-fault evictions (Chart A)
rules.requirement: For a no-fault eviction, relocation assistance is paid per unit: Eligible households receive $11,000 (tenancy under 3 years) or $14,400 (3 or more years, or low income at or below 80% AMI); Qualified households receive $23,150 or $27,400 respectively. If more than one amount applies, the landlord pays the higher amount.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced for a no-fault reason from RSO or JCO units. Qualified tenants are those 62 or older, handicapped or disabled, or with minor dependent children on the date of service of the termination notice; all other tenants are eligible tenants. Low income means 80 percent or less of Area Median Income.
rules.exemptions: The amounts do not apply if the reason for eviction is demolition of a Protected Unit for new construction and the tenant is lower-income (80% AMI or lower).
rules.citation: Relocation Assistance Bulletin A, Chart A (LAHD #33A – 07/01/2026)
rules.quoted_span: The relocation amounts above apply if a tenant is displaced for a no-fault reason described on page 1 of this bulletin.

rules.title: Reduced relocation assistance for Mom and Pop properties
rules.requirement: Mom and Pop property owners may pay reduced relocation assistance for a good faith eviction for occupancy by the owner or an eligible relative, if all conditions in LAMC 151.30 are met. The reduced amounts are $10,550 for eligible households and $21,250 for qualified households.
rules.coverage_text: Evictions for occupancy by the owner or an eligible relative where the building has four or fewer rental units, the landlord has not used this provision in the previous three years, the landlord owns no more than four units of residential property and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City of Los Angeles, and the eligible relative does not own residential property in the City of Los Angeles.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for JCO single-family dwellings owned by natural persons
rules.requirement: When a single-family dwelling subject to the JCO is owned by a natural person who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City, relocation assistance is one month's rent in effect when the termination notice was served, paid as money or credit.
rules.coverage_text: Single-family dwellings subject to the JCO owned by a natural person (including through a trust or registered legal entity controlled by that person) who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: When the residential real property  is a single-family dwelling subject to the JCO and the owner is a natural person, including natural  persons who hold properties in a trust or registered legal entity controlled by   that natural person, who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot  in the City of Los Angeles: one month’s rent that was in effect when   the landlord served the written notice to terminate the tenancy, as either a monetary payment or credit.
rules.interaction_text: The Los Angeles Municipal Code Section 151.30(E) shall not apply.

rules.title: Timing and method of relocation assistance payments
rules.requirement: Relocation assistance must be made available within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice of eviction, split equally among multiple tenants in a unit. The landlord may instead deposit the funds in an escrow account within the 15-day period, with payments for actual relocation expenses made within three (3) working days of a request.
rules.key_value: Within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice
rules.coverage_text: Landlords owing relocation assistance for no-fault evictions under the RSO or JCO.

rules.title: Termination for demolition for new construction of a Protected Unit
rules.requirement: A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish for new construction must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict (JCO) or Notice of Intent to Withdraw (RSO) with LAHD, serve a written notice and file a copy with LAHD within 3 business days, and pay relocation under the Housing Crisis Act or City laws, whichever is higher. City laws require RSO or JCO amounts within 15 days of serving the notice, enhanced for lower income tenants.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies in Protected Units covered by the RSO or JCO being terminated for demolition for new construction; all RSO units are Protected Units.
rules.exemptions: The regular RSO or JCO relocation rules apply if the units to be demolished are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish for new construction is required to pay relocation assistance and to file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental Housing Use with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) prior to evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).
rules.interaction_text: Pay relocation assistance to tenants in compliance with the State law’s Housing Crisis Act (California Government Code Section 66300 et seq.) or the City laws, whichever is higher.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation requirements and standardized payments
rules.requirement: Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction within 5 years after filing the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict must comply with RPO relocation rules, choosing one of 3 options and paying the highest applicable State or City amount. Under the standardized payment option, lower income households receive $115,480 (extremely low), $96,750 (very low) or $87,450 (low income).
rules.key_value: Extremely Low Income $115,480; Very Low Income $96,750; Low Income $87,450 (Effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027)
rules.coverage_text: Protected Units demolished for the purpose of new construction; enhanced standardized payments apply only to Low, Very Low and Extremely Low Income households.
rules.exemptions: The RPO only applies to Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction. Households above low income are paid under Chart A (RSO or JCO amounts).
rules.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.quoted_span: Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to comply with relocation requirements under the RPO. Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.interaction_text: The owner must pay the highest of the applicable relocation amounts to comply with State and City laws.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance occupant protections
rules.requirement: For Protected Units demolished for new construction, the RPO gives occupants a right to relocation, a right to remain up to 6 months before construction starts (including a 6-month notice to move out), a right to return if demolition does not proceed, a right of first refusal for some tenants, and tenant notification requirements.
rules.coverage_text: Occupants of Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction.
rules.quoted_span: The RPO’s occupant protections include: 1) Right to Relocation, 2) Right to Remain in the unit up to 6 months prior to start of construction activities, which includes a 6-month notice to move out, 3) Right to Return to the same unit if the demolition does not proceed, 4) Right of First Refusal to the new building for some tenants and 5) Tenant Notification Requirements.
rules.interaction_text: On February 11, 2025, the Los Angeles City Council adopted the RPO which codified and expanded upon replacement requirements and occupant protections of the HCA, and enhanced requirements for Restricted Affordable Units.
